_comment: Lane F SaaS-integration governance control map (Vol IX Book 05). Onboarding a third-party SaaS is not one control event — it is the moment 24 controls are closed at the workflow plane, or silently skipped. The lifecycle: request -> verify authorization -> classify the flow -> agree (ISA) -> register as a CI -> configure SSO -> issue+rotate credentials -> enable SCIM -> assign least privilege -> propagate JML -> log -> attest -> offboard. Actuation via Graph through the in-boundary MID; ServiceNow governs who/when/approval/evidence. Per the Vol 0 Book 02 convention, Vol VII/IX closures are where a control is COORDINATED, EVIDENCED and OPERATED — the architecture volumes own the primary closure; this lane is the workflow plane. Each item carries `phase` and `summary`: the Book 06 catalog tables are RENDERED from these by render_book_catalog.py and drift-gated, so the book cannot hand-drift from this map. Projection of aan-compliance-spine.yml, CI-validated against it (slots, KSI themes, boundary, schema) by validate_day2_control_maps.py. Scope: FedRAMP Moderate + GCC Moderate.

saas.request.title: Request a SaaS integration
saas.request.summary: Records the SaaS, its business owner, the business need, and **the specific identity attributes it will receive**. That last field is what makes classification possible; without it, exposure gets reasoned about from vendor marketing
saas.request.note: Captures the SaaS, its business owner, the business need, and THE SPECIFIC IDENTITY ATTRIBUTES IT WILL RECEIVE. That last field is what makes saas.classify possible — without it nobody can reason about exposure except from vendor marketing. This is the record of which organizational data leaves the boundary, to which external system: the outbound direction that inbound-scoped external-access controls never reach.
saas.request.actuator_gap: Lane F actuator not yet implemented: no SaaS provisioning client (gallery app / SCIM sync-job / federation) and no ACME credential client exists in script-includes/. The control map is declared; the code is not written.

saas.verify.authorization.title: Record the FedRAMP authorization verdict
saas.verify.authorization.summary: **The gate.** A FedRAMP Marketplace verdict at or above the Moderate baseline, recorded against the request. No verdict, no progression
saas.verify.authorization.note: THE GATE. A FedRAMP Marketplace verdict at or above the Moderate baseline, recorded against the request BEFORE anything is configured. No verdict, no progression. The verdict is an ISSO decision recorded by a human — the inventory tooling narrows the queue and never emits an 'unauthorized' finding, because name-matching a gallery display name to a marketplace offering is unreliable. A verdict collected after configuration is a rationalization, not a gate.
saas.verify.authorization.actuator_gap: Lane F actuator not yet implemented: no SaaS provisioning client (gallery app / SCIM sync-job / federation) and no ACME credential client exists in script-includes/. The control map is declared; the code is not written.

saas.verify.interfaces.title: Record the CSO's functions, ports, protocols and endpoints
saas.verify.interfaces.summary: The CSO's SSO/SCIM endpoints, ports and protocols recorded; the NGFW allow-list and DDI records derive from this, so an undocumented endpoint is drift
saas.verify.interfaces.note: The SaaS declares its endpoints (SSO ACS URL, SCIM base URL, IdP-initiated targets) and the protocols in use. The NGFW allow-list and the DDI/DNS records for the integration derive from this record rather than from a ticket comment — so an undocumented endpoint is detectable as drift.

saas.classify.title: Classify the outbound flow — assertion or standing replica
saas.classify.summary: Assertion-only or standing replica? Derived from the attributes captured at request, not judged ad hoc
saas.classify.note: SSO-only passes an assertion at sign-in and is gone. SCIM leaves a durable, continuously synced replica of directory data in the vendor cloud. Derived from the attributes captured at saas.request, not judged ad hoc. This classification decides whether saas.isa applies — collapsing the two is the most expensive modelling error available here.

saas.isa.title: Attach an ISA before enabling synchronization
saas.isa.summary: SCIM path only — an ISA attached and approved **before** the sync job is enabled
saas.isa.note: SCIM path only. A standing directory replica in an external system is an interconnection, and an interconnection needs an agreement — attached and approved BEFORE the sync job is enabled, not after it works. SSO-only integrations skip this entirely and must not be made to wait for it: over-gating the cheap path is how a control gets routed around.

saas.approve.summary: Requester may never approve. Privileged scope or any SCIM path requires a security approver distinct from the owner
saas.approve.note: Requester may never be approver. Any integration receiving privileged scopes, or any SCIM path, requires a security approver distinct from the business owner. Enforced pre-flight by EntraHelpdeskGate, not by convention.

saas.register.ci.title: Register the integration as a reconciled CI
saas.register.ci.summary: The service principal, its gallery template id, SSO mode and sync-job state become a CMDB CI **reconciled to the authoritative IPAM/DDI asset identity** (the CM-8 join key, Book 01). An integration absent from the register is drift
saas.register.ci.note: The service principal, its applicationTemplateId, its SSO mode and its sync-job state become a CMDB CI reconciled to the authoritative IPAM/DDI asset identity (the CM-8 join key, Vol VII Book 01). DDI stays the SSOT; the CMDB is the workflow projection. An integration absent from the CI register is drift, which is what makes an un-governed portal click detectable at all.

saas.change.note: Every compliance-affecting change to the integration — enabling SSO, enabling SCIM, widening scope, rotating a credential — carries an approved, reviewable change record before actuation. This is the Vol VII Book 00 coordination doctrine applied unchanged.

saas.sso.configure.title: Configure federated SSO; forbid local app accounts
saas.sso.configure.summary: Federation actuated via Graph through the MID Server — never a portal click. Records that SaaS-local credentials are disabled or exception-approved: *"SSO available" is not "SSO required"*
saas.sso.configure.note: SAML or OIDC federation actuated via Graph through the in-boundary MID Server — never a portal click. The catalog item also records that local/native credentials on the SaaS side are disabled or explicitly exception-approved: 'SSO available' is not 'SSO required', and only the second closes anything.

saas.identifier.summary: One enterprise identifier per person from the HR-derived worker record (Book 04). The vendor never mints its own identifier for an organizational user
saas.identifier.note: One enterprise identifier per person carried into the SaaS, sourced from the HR-derived worker record (Vol I Book 04). Prevents per-app identity sprawl and makes rehire/transfer correlation possible in the target system. The SaaS never mints its own identifier for an organizational user.

saas.credential.issue.title: Issue the federation credential — short-lived
saas.credential.issue.summary: Certificate-based where the SaaS supports it; a secret with a **mandatory expiry** where it does not. No long-lived secret in configuration
saas.credential.issue.note: The SAML token-signing certificate and the SCIM bearer token are authenticators with lifecycles, not setup steps. Certificate-based where the SaaS supports it; a secret with a MANDATORY expiry where it does not. No long-lived secret in config — same rule as Vol IX Book 03 Lane E, applied to the federation trust.
saas.credential.issue.actuator_gap: Lane F actuator not yet implemented: no SaaS provisioning client (gallery app / SCIM sync-job / federation) and no ACME credential client exists in script-includes/. The control map is declared; the code is not written.

saas.credential.rotate.title: Rotate the federation credential before expiry
saas.credential.rotate.summary: Automated rotation ahead of expiry, SaaS-side update tracked as a change. The trust never depends on a human remembering a three-year certificate
saas.credential.rotate.note: Automated rotation ahead of expiry, with the SaaS-side update tracked as a change. The integration never depends on a human remembering a 3-year certificate. An expiring signing certificate is the single most common cause of a federation outage, which makes this the control with the strongest operational ally.

saas.pki.note: Issuance, publication to the SaaS relying party, rollover and revocation of the token-signing certificate under the agency certificate policy — rather than Entra's default self-signed 3-year certificate accepted silently at setup.

saas.scim.enable.summary: Creating the sync job **is** automated account management. Blocked until `saas.isa` is approved. Scoping filter and attribute mapping ride in the change record, so *which attributes leave* is reviewable, not discovered later
saas.scim.enable.note: Creating the synchronization job IS automated account management: accounts in the SaaS are created, updated and removed from the authoritative directory rather than by hand. Blocked until saas.isa is approved. The scoping filter and attribute mapping are part of the change record, so 'which attributes leave' is reviewable, not discovered later.

saas.leaver.title: Propagate separation to the SaaS
saas.leaver.summary: The separation event drives disable/remove in the SaaS **on the effective date**, evidenced per step. Separation-to-revocation interval inside the SaaS becomes a ConMon metric
saas.leaver.note: The HR separation event (Vol I Book 04 owns the fact; PS-4) drives disable/remove in the SaaS on the effective date, evidenced per step. Separation-to-revocation interval in the SaaS becomes a ConMon metric. Without this, the directory is clean and the SaaS still has a live account — the exact failure an assessor probes.

saas.offboard.title: Terminate the integration and revoke the trust
saas.offboard.summary: Disable the sync job, remove assignments, revoke the trust and credential, confirm vendor-side deletion against the retention record, retire the CI
saas.offboard.note: Disable the sync job, remove assignments, revoke the federation trust and the credential, confirm vendor-side deletion against the retention record, retire the CI. The step most often skipped: an integration nobody uses still holds a live directory replica and a valid signing certificate. Triggered by attestation failure, business-need lapse, or a withdrawn FedRAMP authorization.
